title: Catalyst efficiency — diagnose first
plainEnglish: The downstream oxygen sensor looks too much like the upstream one. The computer thinks the catalytic converter on bank 1 is not cleaning the exhaust. That can be a dying brick — or an exhaust leak, a lazy upstream sensor, or a misfire that poisoned it.
doNotThrow: Do not buy a catalytic converter from P0420 alone. A converter is $800–$2,500. A sensor or a clamp is not. Graph both O2 sensors and leak-check the exhaust before anyone orders a brick.

diy.why: You can read the code and listen for an exhaust tick. Graphing sensors and a smoke / soapy-water leak check is shop work.
steps: Write the exact code. If the scanner shows freeze-frame, photograph RPM, load, mph, and coolant temp.
Listen for a tick and smell for exhaust in the cabin. A leak in front of the downstream sensor fakes a dead cat.
Do not authorize a converter from this page. The aisle card for the brick is stamped HOLD.
tools: Eyes and ears under the car

shop.why: Ask for the graph and the leak check before they price the brick. Diagnosis is a line. The converter is a different line.
say: I have P0420 stored. I want freeze-frame and a leak check before anyone prices a converter.
Show me upstream vs downstream O2. If they look the same after a leak check, then we talk brick.

aisleQuestions.why: Bank 1 and the converter change with the engine family. V6 vs I4 is a different box.
Converters are emissions-family parts. The wrong one will not pass a smog check.
Usually does not change the cat. Still ask so they do not pull an exhaust for a different chassis.

parts.label: Upstream O2 / AFR sensor (Bank 1)
parts.note: Only if the graph is lazy. Not automatic from the code.

parts.label: Downstream O2 sensor (Bank 1)
parts.note: The monitor sensor. A failed heater or a lazy signal can fake a dead brick.

parts.label: Exhaust gasket / flex leak
parts.note: A leak in front of the downstream sensor looks like a dead cat.

parts.label: Catalytic converter (Bank 1)
parts.note: HOLD. Diagnose first. Do not throw this part from P0420 alone.

title: Catalyst efficiency Bank 2
plainEnglish: Same catalyst-efficiency story on the other bank. Same rule: prove the brick, do not assume it. Do not replace both converters because one bank set a code.
doNotThrow: Do not pair-replace converters from P0430. Graph Bank 2 only. A leak or a lazy sensor still wins.

diy.why: Same as P0420. Write the code. Do not buy two bricks.
steps: Confirm it is P0430, not P0420. Bank 2 is the other exhaust path.
Do not authorize a 'both cats while we are in there' line from one bank.

shop.why: Same graph-and-leak check as P0420, Bank 2 only.
say: This is Bank 2. I want the same O2 graph and leak check — not both converters.

aisleQuestions.why: Bank 2 only exists on some layouts. An inline-four may not have a Bank 2 cat the way a V6 does.
Wrong emissions family fails smog even if it bolts up.

parts.label: Upstream O2 (Bank 2)
parts.note: Only if the Bank 2 graph is lazy.

parts.label: Catalytic converter (Bank 2)
parts.note: HOLD. Same diagnose-first rule as P0420.

title: Random / multiple misfire
plainEnglish: The computer counted misfires on more than one cylinder. That can be plugs, coils, a vacuum leak, fuel, or a failing coil driver. A flashing light means stop driving — raw fuel is washing the cat.
doNotThrow: Do not throw a coil kit from P0300. Name the cylinder that is dead, then the part that failed the test.

diy.why: You can read pending codes (P0301–P0308) and look at plug condition. Swap-test is shop or experienced DIY.
steps: If the light is flashing, stop driving. That is catalyst-poisoning territory.
Write every code, including pending P0301–P0308. Those name the hole.
Do not buy four coils because the aisle had a kit.

shop.why: Ask which cylinder and which test. A coil swap that moves the misfire is a sentence. A kit is a guess.
say: P0300 is a pattern, not a parts list. Which cylinder, and did a coil swap move it?

aisleQuestions.why: Coil-on-plug vs a shared coil pack changes the box they pull.
Gap and heat range are engine-family parts. The wrong plug is a new misfire.

parts.label: Spark plugs (set)
parts.note: If they are due or look fouled. Not automatic from P0300.

parts.label: Ignition coil (the dead hole)
parts.note: One coil if a swap-test moved the misfire. Not a four-pack by default.

parts.label: Plug wires (if equipped)
parts.note: Coil-on-plug cars do not have a wire set. Ask first.

title: System too lean (Bank 1)
plainEnglish: The computer is adding fuel because the exhaust looks lean. Unmetered air (vacuum leak, cracked hose, dirty MAF) beats a new oxygen sensor most days.
doNotThrow: Do not throw a MAF or an O2 from P0171. Find the hiss or the fuel trim number first.

diy.why: You can listen for a vacuum hiss and check the air-box lid. A smoke machine is shop gear.
steps: Confirm the air-box lid is latched and the intake tube is not cracked.
Listen for a hiss at idle. Do not spray starter fluid around a hot exhaust.

shop.why: Ask for short-term and long-term fuel trim at idle and 2500 rpm. A leak shows at idle. A fuel problem shows under load.
say: I have P0171. I want fuel trims at idle and 2500, and a leak location — not a MAF by default.

aisleQuestions.why: Intake boots and PCV valves are engine-family parts.

parts.label: Intake tube / boot
parts.note: A cracked boot after the MAF is classic unmetered air.

parts.label: PCV valve / hose
parts.note: A stuck-open PCV leans the idle.

parts.label: MAF sensor
parts.note: HOLD until trims and a leak check say the meter is lying.

title: EVAP large leak
plainEnglish: The vapor-recovery system failed a large-leak test. A loose or cracked gas cap still causes this. A canister is the last box, not the first.
doNotThrow: Do not authorize a charcoal canister from the code alone. Click the cap. Then a smoke test with a leak location.
minutes: Cap check tonight · smoke test if it returns

diy.why: The cap is a driveway part. If the light returns after three drive cycles, the shop smoke-tests.
steps: Click the cap until it rattles. Look at the seal — cracked rubber is a $15 part.
Clear the code if your scanner can, or let it go out after a few honest trips.
If it comes back, you want a smoke-test photo, not a canister quote.

shop.why: Smoke test with a location in inches from a named part. 'Needs a canister' without a leak is a stall.
say: I already clicked the cap. If it returns I want a smoke-test location, not a canister by default.

aisleQuestions.ask: Tethered cap or a screw cap?
aisleQuestions.why: Some cars use a capless neck. The 'cap' is a different box.

parts.label: Gas cap
parts.note: First part. Click it. Replace it if the seal is cracked.

parts.label: Purge / vent valve
parts.note: After a smoke test names it.

parts.label: EVAP charcoal canister
parts.note: HOLD. Last, not first.

title: Coolant temp below thermostat
plainEnglish: The engine is not reaching the temperature the thermostat is supposed to open at. A stuck-open thermostat is the usual part. A low coolant level or a lying temp sensor is the other story.
doNotThrow: Do not throw a water pump from P0128. Check the first-running temp and the coolant level.

diy.why: On many fours this is a driveway job if you can catch the drained coolant. Housing-integrated stats are messier.
steps: Check the overflow is between the marks when cold.
If you replace the stat, match the temperature rating stamped on the old one.
Bleed the system the way the manual says — trapped air is a new overheat.

shop.why: Ask for the opening temperature on the box and the coolant spec. A 'flush package' is a different line.
say: P0128. I want the thermostat and the factory coolant — not a cooling-system upsell.

aisleQuestions.why: Housing vs in-hose thermostat. The box changes.
Mixing chemistries gels. The bay ticket should name the spec, not the color.

parts.label: Thermostat (or housing)
parts.note: Match the opening temperature. Some cars sell the housing as a unit.

parts.label: Engine coolant
parts.note: The spec on the ticket, not 'whatever is green.'

parts.label: Thermostat gasket / O-ring
parts.note: Often in the box. Ask before they add a second SKU.

title: Cabin air filter
plainEnglish: This is the filter that cleans the air you breathe. It lives behind the glove box on most cars. Shops charge $80–$120 for a 10-minute clip job. If the AC smells like a wet sock or the windshield fogs, look here first.
doNotThrow: Do not pay an hour of labor for a clip job you can do in the driveway. If they already opened it, you want the old filter in a bag and the part at cost.

diy.why: Most drop the glove box. Photograph the airflow arrow before you pull the old one.
steps: Search this car plus cabin filter location, or open the manual. Most drop the glove box.
Empty the glove box. Squeeze the sides past the stops or unclip the damper.
Open the plastic door. Photograph the old filter so you know which way the arrow pointed.
Slide the old one out. Vacuum leaves and grit from the housing.
Install the new filter with the arrow matching the housing mark. Clip the door and glove box back.

shop.why: If they already charged cabin-filter labor, ask to see the old filter. An $80 labor line on a clip job is the classic pad.
say: I will replace the cabin filter myself. If you already have it open, I only want the part at cost — not an hour of labor.
Text me a photo of the old cabin filter in your hand. Then give me the parts-plus-labor number.

aisleQuestions.why: Two boxes on the same hook. Charcoal is the odor one. Same size, different price.
A few cars have two cabin sizes across the same year. The counter will still ask.

parts.label: Cabin air filter
parts.note: One part. Match year, make, model. Arrow toward the blower.

title: Engine air filter
plainEnglish: The engine air filter sits in a black plastic box in the engine bay. A clogged one makes the car feel tired. Pop the clips, photograph the old one, drop the new one in the same orientation.
doNotThrow: Do not let them sell a MAF cleaning as a required add-on to an air-filter swap.

diy.why: Clips or a few screws. Seat the lid or you invent a lean code.
steps: Pop the air-box clips. Photograph the old filter so the new one faces the same way.
Wipe grit out of the box. Do not blow dirt into the MAF.
Seat the lid until every clip is home.

shop.why: This is a counter part, not a labor hour.
say: I am buying the engine air filter. I will install it.

aisleQuestions.why: Two engines in the same year often use two boxes.

parts.label: Engine air filter
parts.note: One panel or one round element. Confirm the shape against the old one.

title: Oil and filter
plainEnglish: Drain the sump, spin a new filter, fill the viscosity on the door sticker. The counter will ask for the spec, not 'regular oil.'
doNotThrow: Do not accept 'whatever we have' if the door sticker names a dexos / dexos1 / 0W-20. A flush additive is a different line.

diy.why: If you can get it on stands and torque the drain plug, this is a driveway job. Hot oil burns. Catch the filter gasket.
steps: Read the viscosity and capacity on the garage ticket or the door sticker.
Drain warm, not scalding. Replace the crush washer if the car uses one.
Spin the new filter hand-tight plus the spec. Fill, idle, recheck the stick.

shop.why: LOF is fine. Shop supplies and a flush package are the pad. Ask for the viscosity in writing.
say: Door-sticker viscosity and the filter. No flush unless you can name what failed.

aisleQuestions.why: Capacity and filter thread change with the engine.
0W-20 vs 5W-30 is not a vibe. It is the door sticker.

parts.label: Oil filter
parts.note: Cartridge vs spin-on. Confirm the housing.

parts.label: Engine oil
parts.note: Buy the viscosity and the spec, then the quart count.

parts.label: Drain-plug washer
parts.note: If the plug uses a crush washer, replace it.

title: Brake pads
plainEnglish: Indicator squeal is a thin pad. Metal-on-metal is a rotor. Ask for millimeters remaining, not 'they're due.' Front and rear are different boxes.
doNotThrow: Do not buy rotors because the pad squealed. Measure the pad and the rotor. Hardware kits stop the rattle that gets blamed on pads.

diy.why: If you can torque lug nuts to the door sticker and seat the caliper pins, this is weekend work. A seized slider is a different job.
steps: Measure pad thickness. Under about 3 mm is a conversation. Metal-on-metal is today.
Front or rear? They are different SKUs.
Torque wheels to the door sticker in a star. Bed the pads the way the box says.

shop.why: Ask for pad mm and rotor thickness vs minimum. 'While we are in there' on unused rears needs a number.
say: How many millimeters on the inner pad? What is the rotor vs the discard spec?

aisleQuestions.why: Two different boxes. Do not let them pull both until you said both.
Some trucks use different front pads or a different caliper on 4WD.
Performance packages change the pad shape.

parts.label: Brake pads (one axle)
parts.note: Name the axle. Ceramic vs semi-met is a noise and dust choice.

parts.label: Pad hardware kit
parts.note: Clips and abutment hardware. Cheap insurance against a squeal comeback.

parts.label: Brake rotors
parts.note: HOLD unless they are below discard, grooved, or pulsating. Squeal alone is not a rotor.

title: 12-volt battery
plainEnglish: A weak 12-volt battery is a click or a slow crank. The counter will ask for the group size and whether it is top-post or side-post. An EV still has this battery.
doNotThrow: Do not throw an alternator from a slow crank until someone measured cranking voltage and charging voltage.

diy.why: If you can get the hold-down off and you register the new battery when the car requires it, this is a driveway job. Memory savers are optional.
steps: Match group size, terminal layout, and CCA — not just 'the silver one.'
Negative off first, negative on last.
Some cars need a registration or a window-auto reset. Ask before you leave the aisle.

shop.why: Ask for the load-test number and charging voltage. A battery they just sold should still show the printout.
say: What was cranking voltage, and what is the alternator at idle and 2000 rpm?

aisleQuestions.why: H6 vs 35 vs 51R is the box. Year/make/model gets you close; the tray decides.
Start-stop and bigger engines want a different AGM.

parts.label: 12V battery
parts.note: Group size and terminal layout. AGM if the car came with AGM.

parts.label: Battery terminals / ends
parts.note: If the old ends are green and crumbling.

title: Wiper blades
plainEnglish: Driver and passenger are often two lengths. Beam vs hook is the other question. This is a parking-lot job.
doNotThrow: Do not pay labor to click two blades on.

diy.why: Lift the arm. Read the clip. Do not let the arm slam the glass.
steps: Buy the pair that matches this car. Driver is usually longer.
Lift the arm, release the old clip, click the new one until it locks.
Rest the arm. Spray washer fluid and watch one sweep.

shop.why: Counter part. If they install, it should be minutes, not a line on the RO.
say: I am buying the blades. I will click them on.

aisleQuestions.why: Two SKUs on many cars. A hatch may have a third.

parts.label: Wiper blades (pair)
parts.note: Confirm hook vs pinch vs bayonet before you leave the aisle.

title: Spark plugs
plainEnglish: Plugs are an interval part on a lot of engines and a diagnosis part on a misfire. Gap, reach, and heat range have to match. Coil-on-plug means the coil comes off first.
doNotThrow: Do not throw coils because the plugs were due. Do not use a 'universal' plug that needs a different gap.

diy.why: If you can reach them and you torque to spec, yes. Cross-threaded plugs in aluminum heads are an expensive afternoon.
steps: Blow dirt out of the wells before the old plugs come out.
Gap only if the box says to. Many iridium plugs are pre-gapped.
Torque. Anti-seize only if the manufacturer says so.

shop.why: Ask for the heat range and whether they gapped. A 'tune-up kit' that adds wires you do not have is a pad.
say: Factory plug. Torque to spec. I do not want a coil kit unless a cylinder failed a swap-test.

aisleQuestions.why: Reach and heat range change with the engine family.

parts.label: Spark plugs (set)
parts.note: Buy the count for this engine. Confirm iridium vs platinum.

parts.label: Coil boots / grease
parts.note: If the boots tore coming off.

title: Shocks / struts
plainEnglish: A dead shock bounces more than once after a driveway. Struts are a spring-and-damper unit on many cars. The counter will ask 2WD or 4WD before they walk the aisle.
doNotThrow: Do not buy four corners because one leaked. Measure the leak and the bounce. Springs are a different part if the car sits low.

diy.why: A loaded strut compressor can kill you. Complete assemblies are safer for weekend work, still need a torque sequence and an alignment.
steps: Push a corner. More than one bounce is a clue, not a diagnosis.
Look for wet dampers. Dust is not oil.
Budget an alignment after struts.
tools: None for the check. A shop for the spring.

shop.why: Ask complete assembly vs bare damper. Ask 2WD or 4WD on the RO. Alignment is a separate line.
say: This is [2WD or 4WD]. I want the application in writing and an alignment after, not 'we will see.'

aisleQuestions.why: Different mounting, different box. This is the question that stops a wrong strut from leaving the aisle.
Four different SKUs on a lot of trucks.
HD and police packages change the spring rate.

parts.label: Strut or shock (name the corner)
parts.note: Complete assembly vs bare. 2WD/4WD first.

parts.label: Strut mount / bearing
parts.note: If they are not in the complete assembly.

title: CV axle
plainEnglish: A torn boot throws grease. A worn outer joint clicks on a full-lock turn. Inner joints clunk on takeoff. 2WD vs 4WD changes the shaft they pull.
doNotThrow: Do not buy two axles because one boot ripped. The quiet side can wait if the boot is intact.

diy.why: Hub nut torque and a stubborn spline are how weekend jobs become tow trucks. Experienced DIY with a torque spec can do it.
steps: Confirm which corner clicks. Full-lock left vs right names the outer joint.
Look for grease on the inside of the wheel. That is a boot, not always a dead joint yet.
tools: None for the look. A torque spec if you turn wrenches.

shop.why: Ask left or right, inner or outer, 2WD or 4WD. A 'pair' is a sales sentence.
say: One axle. Tell me left or right and 2WD or 4WD. I do not want the pair unless the other boot is open.

aisleQuestions.why: Different shafts. This is the parts-person question.
They are not always the same length.
Automatic vs manual and engine torque change the joint.

parts.label: CV axle (one side)
parts.note: Name the side and 2WD/4WD before they walk away.

parts.label: Axle / hub nut
parts.note: Many are one-time torque nuts.

title: Starter
plainEnglish: A single loud click with a good battery is often the starter solenoid. Silence can still be a security, a neutral switch, or a fusible link. The counter will ask the engine — some starters hide under the intake.
doNotThrow: Do not throw a starter from a dead battery. Measure voltage at the starter while someone cranks.

diy.why: Access is ugly on a lot of transverse engines. Voltage at the terminal is the DIY check.
steps: Load-test the 12V first.
If the lights stay bright and you get one click, the starter is on the list — after voltage at the post.

shop.why: Ask for voltage at the starter during the crank. A rebuilt vs new is a warranty conversation.
say: Battery tested good. What was voltage at the starter while cranking?

aisleQuestions.why: Mount and tooth count change. Some need the intake off.
Rarely changes the starter. Still ask on trucks so they do not pull a 4WD skid-plate kit you do not need.

parts.label: Starter
parts.note: After the battery and voltage-at-the-post check.

title: Alternator
plainEnglish: A charging system should sit around 13.5–14.7 V with the engine running. A battery light is a pointer, not a parts list. A slipping belt can fake a dead alternator.
doNotThrow: Do not throw an alternator from a battery light until someone measured charging voltage and looked at the belt.

diy.why: Voltage is the driveway test. The swap is often a belt-and-bracket puzzle.
steps: Measure across the battery at idle and at 2000 rpm with loads on.
Look at the belt. Glazing and a screaming pulley are not an alternator.

shop.why: Ask for the voltage number and whether the pulley is a decoupler. Those are a different SKU.
say: What was charging voltage at idle and 2000 rpm? Is the pulley a decoupler?

aisleQuestions.why: Amperage and pulley change with the engine.

parts.label: Alternator
parts.note: After a voltage number. Confirm amperage and pulley.

parts.label: Serpentine belt
parts.note: If it is glazed or they have the tensioner off anyway.

title: No-start sort
plainEnglish: Silence, a click, a crank-no-fire, and a start-and-die are four different aisles. Start at the 12-volt battery. Do not buy a starter, a pump, and a computer on the same ticket.
doNotThrow: Do not throw a parts cannon. Name the symptom: click, crank, or silence. Then one test.

diy.why: You can jump-pack a weak 12V and smell for fuel. After that, stop guessing.
steps: Interior lights bright? If they die when you turn the key, charge or replace the 12V first.
One click: battery or starter circuit. Silence: security, neutral switch, or power.
Cranks but will not fire: fuel, spark, or immobilizer — not a starter.

shop.why: Ask them to name the symptom and the first test. A no-start 'diagnosis' that starts with three parts is a stall.
say: It [clicks / cranks / stays silent]. Test the 12V first. I do not want a starter and a pump on the same guess.

aisleQuestions.why: They will still ask before they pull a starter or a pump.
Access and skid plates change on trucks.

parts.label: 12V battery
parts.note: First part if cranking voltage is down. Not automatic.

parts.label: Starter
parts.note: HOLD until voltage at the post during a click or a silence.

title: Overheating
plainEnglish: A climbing temp gauge is a stop-now problem. Low coolant, a stuck-closed thermostat, a dead fan, or a leaking radiator are the usual list. A head gasket is the expensive end — not the first box.
doNotThrow: Do not throw a water pump or a head gasket from a hot gauge. Find the level, the fan, and whether it overheats at idle or on the highway.

diy.why: You can check a cold level and whether the fans run. A hot cap will scald you.
steps: If it is hot, stop. Cabin heat on high can buy a mile to a shoulder. Do not open a hot cap.
When cold, the overflow should sit between the marks. Empty and hot is a leak or a head.

shop.why: Ask idle vs highway, fan command, and whether combustion gas is in the coolant. A 'head gasket package' without those is a stall.
say: It overheats at [idle / highway]. Check fans and level before anyone prices a head.

aisleQuestions.why: Radiators, stats, and fans are engine-family parts.

parts.label: Thermostat
parts.note: Stuck closed overheats. Stuck open is P0128.

parts.label: Radiator
parts.note: If it is wet or the tanks are swollen. Pressure-test first.

parts.label: Water pump
parts.note: HOLD until a weep or a timing-job access makes it the part.
